sources.title: Cohere Labs Command R+ 08-2024 model card
sources.evidence: Exact August checkpoint: nominal 104 billion parameters; open research weights; CC-BY-NC-4.0 plus acceptable-use policy; text input/output; 128K context; autoregressive Transformer using GQA; RAG and multi-step tools. Reopened October 27, 2026: the exact dated card still explicitly states Model Size 104 billion parameters and describes pretraining followed by SFT and preference training. It does not report active parameters or name a separately sized base checkpoint.

sources.title: Command models get an August refresh
sources.evidence: Release notes dated August 30, 2024 explicitly introduce command-r-plus-08-2024 alongside the Command R refresh.

sources.title: Cohere's Command R+ Model
sources.evidence: Names API ID command-r-plus-08-2024 and specifies 128,000-token context; recommends it for complex RAG and multi-step tool workflows. Plain-text capability extraction loses disabled-icon information.

sources.title: Official Command R+ documentation source
sources.evidence: Read through raw.githubusercontent.com. Exact ID command-r-plus-08-2024 has ToolUse enabled; enabled-capability data excludes Reasoning. This is interpreted with the renderer in s5.

sources.title: Official model capability renderer
sources.evidence: getCapabilities explicitly sets Reasoning disabled when absent from enabledCapabilities, and renders disabled icons crossed out. Together with s4 this establishes a disabled reasoning capability, rather than relying on textual omission.

sources.title: Command A: An Enterprise-Ready Large Language Model
sources.evidence: Later first-party report, released March 28, 2025, compares Command R+ Refresh in benchmark tables. Its architecture section describes Command A; it does not establish a separate active-parameter count for the August R+ checkpoint.

sources.title: Exact checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Configuration access returned HTTP 401 because the checkpoint files are gated. No tensor-level count or additional architecture detail is claimed from this file.

sources.title: Exact checkpoint public architecture metadata
sources.evidence: At revision e808c1a2249354ca211c9f08d1338e5039f633f8, the exact dated checkpoint declares CohereForCausalLM and model_type cohere. Public aggregate tensor metadata is not used as an independently verified learned count. Fresh October 27 metadata returns the same revision and 103,810,674,688 F16 elements. This corroborates the published nominal 104B size; it is not treated as an independently reconstructed learned count or an active count.

sources.title: CohereForCausalLM implementation, Transformers 4.44.2
sources.evidence: The architecture selected by exact checkpoint metadata uses CohereMLP in every decoder layer, with dense gate, up and down projections and no expert router. This establishes dense decoder Transformer classification.

sources.title: Command A: An Enterprise-Ready Large Language Model, revision 2
sources.evidence: Independently inspected the full report freshly fetched October 27, including all parameter references, Command R+ Refresh comparison rows and table headings. Tables compare benchmark performance without an activated-parameter column or a separate active-count definition for the August R+ release. The 111B specification concerns Command A.

sources.title: Introducing Command A+
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The later comparison gives 218B total and 25B active for Command A+ and compares sizes of Command A-family variants. It neither includes the August Command R+ checkpoint in that size table nor defines its active parameters. The newer MoE counts cannot be transferred.

sources.title: Tiny Aya: Bridging Scale and Multilingual Depth
sources.evidence: Independently searched the full report freshly fetched October 27 for Command R+ and active/activated parameter disclosures. No exact-model active count was found. The embedding/non-embedding/total counts in its architecture table concern Tiny Aya, not the August Command R+ checkpoint.

sources.title: Command R+ inference specifications
sources.evidence: Fresh search lead lists 104B total and active. The page identifies the April 4, 2024 release rather than the August revision and provides no field-specific Cohere active-count citation. Its active figure is not adopted as a developer specification.

sources.title: AI progress charts data change
sources.publisher: Independent Hugging Face Space maintained by kaizuberbuehler
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model search found a data row assigning 104 total and 104 active to command-r-plus-08-2024. The row provides no primary citation or active-count derivation and uses repository-creation August 21 as its release date. It is a lead, not a verified Cohere disclosure.

name.note: Official display name; the catalog ID distinguishes the August 2024 revision.

family.note: Catalog family key for the Command R / Command R+ series.

release_date.note: Dated release notes explicitly identify this API revision.

open_weights.note: Research weights are published, subject to the repository's access conditions.

license.note: Weight license; additional acceptable-use terms apply. Hosted API terms are separate.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-card check confirms Cohere's nominal 104B total. Current Hub metadata reports 103.810674688B F16 elements as corroboration; preserve developer precision without requiring a tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh exact-model total, active/activated and named-base searches plus later Cohere comparisons found no separate developer active-count definition. Independent catalogs repeat 104B active without primary attribution; one concerns the earlier April release. The generic pretraining/SFT relationship does not identify a count-bearing base. Dense architecture alone does not establish this field.

architecture.note: Autoregressive dense decoder Transformer with GQA. Exact checkpoint metadata names CohereForCausalLM, whose decoder layers each use dense gated MLP projections without expert routing.

context_window.note: Exact API model's documented context; preserves API units rather than converting 128K to a binary count.

modalities.note: Card explicitly limits both input and output to text.

reasoning.note: Official exact-ID capability data and renderer disable Reasoning. This flag concerns dedicated reasoning support, not general problem-solving ability.

tool_call.note: ToolUse is explicitly enabled for this revision; documentation describes sequential tool calls.

description.value: Cohere's August 2024 Command R+ model for multilingual RAG, long-context text generation, and multi-step tool use
description.note: Replaces subjective workhorse wording with the revision and documented use cases.

patch.description: Cohere's August 2024 Command R+ model for multilingual RAG, long-context text generation, and multi-step tool use
patch.notes: 104B is Cohere's nominal total for the August 2024 checkpoint; active parameters are not separately disclosed. Research weights use CC-BY-NC-4.0 with acceptable-use terms; hosted API terms differ. The reasoning flag describes dedicated thinking-mode support; ordinary text reasoning and tool planning remain supported.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit confirms the nominal 104B total and leaves active parameters undisclosed. Reopened the exact card, documentation and current metadata; searched exact-model and lineage claims; independently checked later Cohere reports and comparisons. Independent 104B-active catalog claims lack a developer counting convention. Added explicit parameter patches and refreshed evidence while preserving unrelated assessments.
notes: Fresh October 27 primary evidence supports the nominal count regardless of prior gated configuration access. No checkpoint shards or repeat tensor census were requested. The Command A full report was read from the shared fresh source cache; later Tiny Aya, Aya Expanse, Aya Vision and Command R7B Arabic report searches produced no August Command R+ active disclosure. Third-party active-count leads are recorded separately from accepted primary evidence.
